answer.rationale: Hard constraint is no increase in delivery risk with the line at 94% and zero buffer and the primary contract lapsing in 14 days without auto-renew. That rules out deferral (c5 was a non-critical service on month-to-month, not this component). Incumbent already refused a price reopen, so negotiate_terms cannot be counted on to both keep supply and hit the 18% cut. A single add_second_source decision would leave the expiring primary unrenewed and put volume on an unproven share. Switching primary is the only path that might cut unit cost (c2) but it cannot be a guarded test when the whole contract dies in 14 days; it would be an immediate full cutover and would increase delivery risk. c1 is the only memory that preserves continuity with no migration and no delivery interruption, so the current intent is renew the incumbent at full volume. Cost mandate will be missed; that finance/downstream-budget risk is flagged. Verifying c2 because its onboarding-speed claim is the only inherited fact that could justify reversing to a switch.
